claims.statement: Although biologics have largely replaced corticosteroids as the cornerstone of medical therapy, the natural history of the disease has not been significantly altered, with up to 80% of patients still requiring surgical intervention at some point in their disease course because of primary and secondary loss of response to biologic medication.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Cited references [1,2] for the 80% surgical rate. Reference [19] for the RCT on early laparoscopic resection vs biologic escalation. The authors note that 90% of CD patients have endoscopic recurrence within 1 year of surgery and up to 35% require repeat resection by 10 years.

claims.evidence_excerpt: Decades of clinical use since the 1960s-70s. The SONIC trial (combination therapy superiority). Side effect data: pancreatitis in ~3%, allergic reactions, bone marrow suppression, liver enzyme abnormalities. Cancer risk: "the risk of lymphoma... is extremely small. claims.statement: The concept of a broad-based pyramid implies that the majority of patients have mild, uncomplicated, and nonprogressive disease. Although many patients will have mild disease 5 years after diagnosis, the long-term clinical course suggests gradual progression toward fibrostenotic and penetrating complications for the majority of patients over time.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Natural history studies showing progressive complications. The TREAT safety registry: concomitant corticosteroid or narcotic use were each associated with increased mortality -- challenging the assumption that "lower" therapies on the pyramid are safer. claims.statement: Infliximab was shown to be effective in inducing and maintaining clinical remission of ulcerative colitis in the ACT-1 and ACT-2 trials.
claims.source_note: [[Yamada 7E - Ch63 UC Clinical Manifestations and Management]]
claims.evidence_excerpt: ACT-1 and ACT-2 (each n=364, placebo vs infliximab 5 or 10 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, 6, then every 8 weeks). Clinical response at week 8: 69.4% (ACT-1) and 64.5% (ACT-2) with 5 mg/kg vs 37.2% and 29.3% with placebo. claims.statement: Measurement of drug concentration and anti-drug antibody levels has been shown to be a cost-effective strategy given the ability to optimize treatment and potentially prevent CD-associated complications.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Trough level thresholds: infliximab >=5 ug/mL, adalimumab >=7.5 ug/mL, certolizumab >=20 ug/mL for clinical remission. claims.statement: Methotrexate is not effective in patients with ulcerative colitis as monotherapy.
claims.source_note: [[Yamada 7E - Ch63 UC Clinical Manifestations and Management]]
claims.evidence_excerpt: Two well-designed RCTs (METEOR and MERIT-UC). The authors explicitly state that "clinical guidelines recommend against the use of methotrexate monotherapy for induction of maintenance in patients with ulcerative colitis."
